notes: §1985:VII.3.4.4 GR3: 'all CODE-SET clauses in the run unit which are associated with that file connector must have the same character set.' The gap of the prior PARTIAL read is closed (kb/Work PB5300): BindCodeSetClause resolves each alphabet-name to its coded character set and records the SET (not the name) in FileModel.FdClauses under FileDescriptionIdentity.CodeSet, and ExternalFileConnectorRules.CheckFileDescriptions, run from Check below COBOL-2002, compares each entry that writes the clause with the first that does and reports COBOL6847; an entry with no clause is skipped, as 1985 constrains only the clauses present. Probed at --std 85 (two programs, one compilation group, an EXTERNAL file written by both and read back): (b) STANDARD-1 against EBCDIC, EBCDIC against STANDARD-1 and STANDARD-2 against STANDARD-1 give COBOL6847 at the second entry, so the shared connector can no longer be written in the last program's code set (the prior read's wrong answer); (d) two alphabet-names for STANDARD-1 (S1, A2), EBCDIC in both, and a clause against none compile and run, reading ABCDE and HELLO back. Between separately compiled elements nothing compares the clause; §1985:I.1.6 leaves a violation's result undefined. The witness uses STD1 and ASCII-CODE, both STANDARD-1. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming kb/Work PB5069 (landed); the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5300 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-09.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-09-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985: "all CODE-SET clauses in the run unit which are associated with that file connector must have the same character set"; 2023: "If any of the file description entries has a CODE-SET clause, all shall have a CODE-SET clause specifying the same character set.". 1985 constrains only the CODE-SET clauses present. 2023 also requires every entry for the external connector to have CODE-SET once any has one, so mixing entries with and without it is refused.
